thesis: Mohnish Pabrai discussed Warren Buffett's admission that only about a dozen of his 58 years of capital allocation decisions were truly good, noting that Berkshire Hathaway's extensive collection of businesses includes many that are marginal or outright mistakes. He highlighted that even the best investors, such as Rakesh Jhunjhunwala, often hold concentrated positions in single companies for decades, suggesting that the investing business is forgiving and that long-term success relies on identifying extraordinary economics rather than frequent trading.
